Lina — following up on Sean's note with specifics to address your checklist. I've included the two artifacts we typically deliver as attachments (audit_harvest_specs.xlsx + chain_of_custody_template.pdf). Below is a compact mapping to your bullets: 

- Export formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) for event records; compressed Parquet for analytical ingest; gzipped tarballs for full-account snapshots. Each file is delivered with a manifest entry: filename, record_count, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, sha256_hash, compressed_size_bytes.

- Export SLAs: For standard requests (<= 90 days of activity) we target 24–48 hours. For large bulk harvests (up to 24 months, multi-terabyte) lead time is typically 3–7 business days depending on retention tier and regional egress constraints. SLA exceptions can be contractually negotiated for Dedicated/Private customers.

- Chain-of-custody & tamper evidence: manifests include per-file SHA-256 and a top-level manifest signed using our KMS (RSA-PSS) with key material protected in HSM. We optionally provide a timestamped attest using an external time-stamping authority (RFC 3161) on request. Delivery receipts include TLS session logs and server-side checksums.

- Redaction & PII controls: exports can be produced with pre-configured redaction templates (PII tokenization, regex-based redaction, field-level suppression). We record what redaction template was applied in the manifest and include a redaction-summary file that lists suppressed fields and counts. Note: redaction is destructive; we produce original, unredacted exports only under legal-preservation orders and with mutually-agreed custody steps.

- Request workflow: export requests are initiated via our secure console (role-based approval). For legal/forensics requests you can nominate a contact that bypasses standard product support queues and routes directly to our Evidence Operations team — we require a company-signed export authorization form and two-factor verification from the requestor.

Lina — quick operational notes from Evidence Ops:

1) For large harvests we prefer delivery to customer-owned S3 using presigned PUTs and a short-lived IAM role for multipart upload. This simplifies chain-of-custody and reduces egress variability.
2) We include a delivery_manifest.sha256 and an accompanying PEM-signed manifest sig (we can provide the public key now if you want to validate)
3) For cross-border data we will segment exports per-region to avoid regulatory egress; please confirm if Acadia requires consolidated delivery or region-segmented packages.
